name: Paddyfield Warbler
rangeDescription: Central eurasia; winters in southern asia
description: Warm brown above and pale below; strong dark eyestripe contrasts with white eyebrow. Smallish reed warbler with long and strongly rounded tail, short bill with dark tip, and short primary projection.

name: African Bare-eyed Thrush
rangeDescription: Arid lowlands of ethiopia and somalia to kenya and northeastern tanzania
description: A distinctive and attractive thrush of dry country, patterned in gray, rufous, and white. Note the orange bill and bare skin around the eye, and the white throat with black striping.

name: White-browed Tit-Spinetail
rangeDescription: Andes of southern peru (apurímac and cusco)
description: Small, active bird found locally in the southern Peruvian Andes. Brownish gray with a red cap, a white-streaked face, breast, and back, and a white eyebrow.

name: Australian Crake
rangeDescription: Moist areas of southeastern and southwestern australia including tasmania
description: Very small, stocky rail with yellow legs and bill. Brown above, blue-gray below black streaking and white specks, barred flanks, and black undertail with a thick white border (unlike Baillon’s Crake, which has fine barring).

name: Maghreb Magpie
rangeDescription: Northeastern mauritania to morocco, algeria, and tunisia
description: The magpie of North Africa; very similar to Eurasian Magpie and closely related. Slightly shorter-winged and longer-tailed than Eurasian Magpie with blue bare skin around the eye.

name: Rufous-fronted Antthrush
rangeDescription: Southeastern peru (madre de dios), adjacent western brazil, and northwestern bolivia
description: Range-restricted antthrush of river’s-edge habitats and bamboo. Grayish brown, with an orange forehead.

name: Cook's Swift
rangeDescription: Lowland myanmar, thailand, vietnam, southern yunnan, and guangxi (southwestern and southeastern china); winters at least to peninsular malaysia
description: Large dark swift with long sickle-shaped wings and a forked tail, which is often kept closed in a needle-tipped point while in flight. Black overall with an ashy gray throat and a thin white rump.

name: Schrenck's Bittern
rangeDescription: Eastern asia; winters to southeastern asia, philippines, and greater sundas
description: Small heron, usually found in reed beds, expansive marshes, and rice fields; can occasionally be found in parks with sheltered areas, particularly lotus ponds and shaded pools. Generally uncommon throughout its range; never in the high densities of Yellow Bittern.

name: Campbell's Fairywren
rangeDescription: Southeastern new guinea (middle strickland river and mount bosavi area)
description: A small, little-known bird limited to lowland and foothill treefall gap regrowth in southwestern Papua New Guinea. Underparts and long, thick eyebrow pale blue.

name: Golden-crested Myna
rangeDescription: Northeastern india to myanmar, thailand (including the northern thai-malay peninsula), and indochina
description: Unmistakable glossy black bird with a dash of bright yellow on the head and wings. Male has more extensive yellow on the head than the female.

name: Matinan Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern sulawesi
description: A chunky, drab flycatcher with a heavy hooked bill. Has a gray head with indistinct pale marking around the eye.

name: Purple Indigobird
rangeDescription: Southwestern angola; kenya, northern and northeastern tanzania, southeastern democratic republic of the congo, southern and eastern zambia, malawi, western mozambique, northeastern botswana, zimbabwe, and northeastern south africa (limpopo and mpumalanga)
description: Nest parasite that lays its eggs in the nests of Jameson’s Firefinch. Breeding males are glossy purplish-black, with a pale brownish panel in the wings, while females and non-breeding males are streaky and brown on the back and pale below, with a bold facial pattern.

name: South Georgia Pipit
rangeDescription: Grassland of south georgia island
description: This small streaky buff-brown ground-dweller is the only resident songbird on South Georgia Island, where it inhabits rocky shorelines, offshore islets, inland pools, and stands of tussac grass. Forages actively for invertebrates, running about and flicking its tail.

name: Rufous-bellied Antwren
rangeDescription: Southern venezuela to the guianas and northeastern amazonian brazil
description: Tiny resident of tall rainforest. Wary and can be difficult to see well; note distinctive sputtering alarm call, tiny size, plain face, and large white (male) or buffy (female) wing spots.

name: Wilson's Phalarope
rangeDescription: Breeds canada and usa; winters in western and southern south america
description: Slender shorebird known for spinning frantically on water to stir up small invertebrates. Note needle-thin bill, longer and thinner than other phalaropes.

name: White-throated Oxylabes
rangeDescription: Dense humid forest of northwestern and eastern madagascar
description: Mid-sized tetraka with a bold white throat and eye-stripe. Brown on the back, rufous on the underparts, and bright rufous on the cap.

name: Desert Owl
rangeDescription: Desert of syria, jordan, arabia, sinai peninsula, and northern egypt
description: A shy, medium-sized owl of desert canyons. Sandy-brown overall with pale underparts and yellow eyes.

name: Scimitar-winged Piha
rangeDescription: Southern peru (cordillera apolobamba of puno) and western bolivia
description: Rare cotinga found along the east slope of the Andes in Bolivia and southern Peru. Plumage is mostly gray with chestnut flanks and rump.

name: Serra do Mar Bristle-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Coastal mountains of southeastern brazil (espírito santo to northern rio grande do sul)
description: Tiny flycatcher with a long slender tail. Differs from other tyrannulets in being mostly bright olive-green above and gray below with darkish ear patches, prominent white eyerings, and pinkish (not dark) legs.

name: Cretzschmar's Bunting
rangeDescription: Southern europe to türkiye; winters to northeastern africa and arabia
description: Very similar to Ortolan Bunting, but note that the base color of the head is gray and not green, and the throat is orange and not yellow. Adult males are brighter and more deeply-colored compared to females and young.
